subject: Production impact: adaptive rate safety-net gap causing sustained throttling
body:
From: Support Ops <ops@novushealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High 429s and latency spike - Novus scheduled batch causing throttling

Marissa,

We started seeing a large spike in 429 responses and elevated p95 latency at 08:55 this morning. This coincided with a nightly scheduled batch from our analytics pipeline. The errors persisted for ~18 minutes and affected our customer-facing widgets.

Attached: traces and screenshots.

Can you confirm if anything changed on your end? This is impacting our morning reports.

--
S. Kaur
Novus Health - Platform Ops
ops@novushealth.com

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ops@novushealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 429s and latency spike - Novus scheduled batch causing throttling

Thanks S. Kaur — I’m looking into this now.

Quick summary: we see a synchronous surge in requests from your account at 08:55 UTC that collided with our adaptive "safety-net" burst policy. The tuned burst threshold for your tier was lower than your expected burst profile (scheduled batches + interactive traffic), which caused sustained token-level throttling rather than short-lived smoothing.

Immediate next steps:
- I’ve opened an internal incident and pulled the request traces (attached).
- Engineering will temporarily raise the burst safety window for Novus while we investigate the policy mismatch.
- I’ll loop in Billing if you need compensation/credits.

Can you share whether the batch schedule changed recently?

—marissa

----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 429s and latency spike - Novus scheduled batch causing throttling

I pulled the policy snapshot. Attach: burst_policy_snapshot_08_17.yaml.

Observations:
- Novus is on dedicated reserved capacity but routing through our global safety-net layer for burst protection. Their configured burst_credit_window is 60s with a max_burst_multiplier of 1.5.
- The incoming traffic shows a steep step increase (approx 8x baseline) for ~16 minutes — that pattern will deplete burst credits quickly and then activate hard throttling.
- There was no recent rollout to the safety-net code path. This looks like a policy configuration mismatch: their tier-level profile doesn’t match the scheduled backfill behavior.

Proposed immediate engineering action:
1) Temporarily bump max_burst_multiplier to 3.0 for Novus and extend burst_credit_window to 300s to absorb the batch.
2) Add a short-term whitelist that bypasses the safety-net for verified scheduled jobs (manual config).
3) Postmortem to add scheduled-batch detection into routing so we can apply transient smoothing automatically.

I’ll stand by for approval to push the config change.

-Karthik

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Exec note: NovusHealth production impact — request for rapid config change and credit consideration

Lauren / Marcus / Grace —

Heads up: NovusHealth (DEAL-4521) experienced a customer-visible incident this morning due to a safety-net burst-policy gap. The short version: scheduled analytics batch caused sustained burst beyond the configured safety parameters and triggered hard throttling (429s) across their session-dependent widgets. Impact window ~08:55–09:13 PDT.

Impact:
- Elevated 429s and p95 latency spikes for a subset (~12%) of user-facing requests.
- Customer has flagged potential churn risk given this is during their report generation window.

What we’re doing now (already underway):
- Engineering (Karthik) is ready to apply a temporary config increase to absorb the batch (bump multiplier and window).
- Placing a short-term bypass for scheduled jobs while we instrument detection.
- Collecting artifacts for a root-cause postmortem (traces, policy snapshot) — attached.

Asks:
- Approval to push the temporary config change now (low-risk, reversible).
- Guidance on customer-facing remediation: Marcus, can we offer a credit and a committed postmortem timeline?
- Grace, please advise if this needs additional exec escalation or cross-functional support (CS/Legal/Billing).

I’ll aim to have a customer note back to Novus within 90 minutes after the config push.

—Marissa

----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec note: NovusHealth production impact — request for rapid config change and credit consideration

Approve the temporary config change. Prioritize safety: log the change and the rollback plan.

Customer-facing remediation: offer a single-month service credit on Novus’ next invoice and commit to a postmortem within 5 business days. Coordinate with Billing for the credit flow — loop in billing@novushealth.com in the customer reply.

Also recommend a short-term account review to re-evaluate their tiering/profile.

-Marcus

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ops@novushealth.com, billing@novushealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 429s and latency spike - Novus scheduled batch causing throttling

S. Kaur / R. Chen —

Thanks for the heads up and apologies for the disruption this morning. Summary and actions we’ve taken: 

What happened: our adaptive safety-net burst policy underestimated the duration and amplitude of your scheduled analytics job. The outcome was rapid depletion of burst credits and short-lived hard throttling across sessionized widgets.

Immediate actions taken:
- We applied a temporary increase to your account-specific burst parameters (max_burst_multiplier -> 3.0; burst_credit_window -> 300s) at 10:25 PDT.
- Enabled a short-term routing bypass for verified scheduled jobs (manual override).
- Collected traces and policy snapshots (attached).

Customer remediation:
- We will issue a credit for one month of service on your next invoice (per Marcus’ approval) and commit a postmortem within 5 business days.

Next steps:
- Karthik will lead a postmortem and propose permanent policy adjustments and detection logic. Target: action plan within 3 business days.
- We’d like to schedule a 30-minute post-incident review with your engineering team to ensure batch windows and routing expectations are aligned. Available times tomorrow between 09:00–12:00 PDT.

Please confirm receipt and whether the batch schedule was changed on your side.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0130

Attachments: request_traces_20260817.ndjson; burst_policy_snapshot_08_17.yaml; support_screenshots.zip

----

On Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -0700 ops@novushealth.com wrote:
> Marissa —
>
> Thanks for the quick turnaround. The batch schedule did not change; it’s a standard daily job. We’d like the post-incident review tomorrow at 09:30 PDT. Please include your engineering lead.
>
> Also confirm when the credit will be reflected.
>
> — S. Kaur

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ops@novushealth.com, billing@novushealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: NovusHealth incident, postmortem and credit confirmation

S. Kaur / R. Chen —

Following up: postmortem draft created (JIRA INF-2237) and Karthik’s remediation plan is attached. We confirmed the credit will be applied to your August invoice; Billing will send a confirmation email to R. Chen today.

Key findings from postmortem draft:
- Root cause: account-level burst profile mismatch for scheduled batch traffic.
- Contributory factor: absence of scheduled-job heuristics in safety-net routing.

Permanent fixes planned:
1) Auto-detection of scheduled batch patterns in routing layer (Q3 deliverable).
2) Account-level burst-profile reclassification during onboarding (policy change).
3) Tooling to simulate scheduled bursts during account onboarding and monthly checks.

Thanks again for working with us on the window. We’ll present the final postmortem in the 09:30 PDT review tomorrow and ship the policy changes on our Q3 roadmap.

—Marissa

Attachments: remediation_plan_INF-2237.pdf
